metric.why: PPAs are how the boom finances new generation and how operators back renewable claims. Nuclear agreements, including restarts and small modular commitments, became the signature deals of the AI era.
metric.definition: Long-term contracts by which operators secure generation, nuclear, solar, wind, or gas, for current and future facilities.

reading.body:
Power purchase agreements have become the primary mechanism by which data center operators finance new generation capacity, with nuclear deals—including reactor restarts and small modular reactor commitments—emerging as the defining infrastructure bet of the AI era.

PPAs bind operators to decades of supply from specific generation sources. This matters because data centers require continuous, reliable power at unprecedented scale. An operator cannot wait for the grid to build capacity on its own timeline. By committing to purchase power, operators de-risk generation projects that would otherwise struggle to secure financing. The proliferation of nuclear PPAs specifically signals that operators believe baseload power, not intermittent renewables alone, will be required to meet sustained AI compute demand.

The data covers what PPAs are and their role in financing generation. It does not specify how many megawatts are currently under contract, which operators hold the largest agreements, or how PPA terms compare across different generation types. It does not measure whether these commitments will actually produce power on schedule or whether they reflect genuine demand or speculative positioning. It shows the financial instrument but not its outcome.
